parallel.requirements: Recognized the prompt as a complete Jinja2 package task requiring source modules, project configuration, import surface, examples/tests, and official acceptance coverage.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned implementation and local verification, then launched a broad 15-child read-only audit workflow for module-slice checking after the main project already passed tests.
parallel.implementation: Built the project from upstream Pallets Jinja 3.2.0.dev, added root API/export hardening, checkout test import support, and type-ignore cleanup while preserving the main template engine behavior.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integrated changes directly in the parent workspace with no child implementation merge; the final text file is empty because the agent process timed out, but the workspace artifact remained present for evaluation.
parallel.verification: Ran local 911-test checks, smoke/spec probes, lint/type checks, and consumed workflow audit results; current official evaluation completed with 911 passed out of 911.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The process timed out during or after the audit phase and some audit children hit transient failures, but no required implementation, integration, or acceptance stage remained unfinished in the delivered artifact.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same broad Jinja2 implementation and packaging requirements from the identical prompt and treated upstream Jinja main as the target baseline.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Kept all work in a single parent trajectory with no delegation, moving sequentially through setup, implementation hardening, verification, cleanup, and final response.
serial.implementation: Copied upstream Pallets Jinja, added the same practical hardening around root exports, version handling, conftest importability, pytest collection, and stale type-ignore cleanup.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Integrated all changes locally in one workspace and returned a final narrative explaining provenance, edits, verification, and limitations.
serial.verification: Ran 911 upstream tests, 81 spec checks, 439 symbol checks, ruff, mypy, docs build, install/import checks, and current official evaluation completed with 911 passed out of 911.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished required work is evidenced at closure; the final response notes pyright and submit-tool limitations, while official evaluation still passed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel saw the same prompt requiring a complete Jinja2 project with source code, packaging, tests, and official evaluation readiness.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial saw the identical prompt and built against the same Jinja2 project requirements and 911-test official target.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirement-level outcome difference is evidenced; both current official evaluations passed all tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent owned implementation, then delegated a late 15-child audit workflow while retaining final workspace ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no workflow or child agents and kept ownership in one trajectory from setup through final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel added audit fan-out after implementation; serial remained linear and avoided child-result lifecycle overhead.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child context was organized as read-only audit slices, so no child-owned implementation interface needed to interoperate with another child output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept context in the parent and documented concrete API/export adjustments in the final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more handoff surface for audit findings, but no cross-agent implementation contract affected the passing artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel copied an upstream Jinja tree, verified it, then edited package root exports and checkout/test robustness before broader checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial copied upstream Jinja, made targeted root API, conftest, pytest, and type-check cleanup changes, and summarized the diff explicitly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The implementation path was materially similar; serial recorded the final diff in narrative form, while parallel spent extra time on child audits.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used one Workflow call, one TaskOutput retrieval, and 15 workflow child logs; workflow results were retrieved without a TaskStop.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no delegation, no child logs, no TaskOutput calls, and no result-join lifecycle to manage.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel carried child-result monitoring overhead; serial avoided that class of lifecycle risk entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel protocol validation shows delegation occurred but no contamination path hits; audit children did not provide implementation writes to merge.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no shared-workspace delegation and its final response describes all local project files integrated in the workspace.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No merge or shared-state failure separates the attempts; parallel shared the workspace for audit observation without evidenced write collision.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had local full-suite checks and its current official evaluation completed successfully with 911 passed and no failures.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial reported broad local verification and its current official evaluation also completed successfully with 911 passed and no failures.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No acceptance difference exists; both reached the same official pass despite different process closure states.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the full agent budget and ended with return code 143 for agent_timeout after using the audit workflow.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed normally with return code 0 in about 900 seconds and returned a final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a process timeout and empty final text, but this closure cost did not change the official task outcome or leave an acceptance-critical task gap.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is not discordant: both current completed status.json evaluation records report solution_passed true with 911 of 911 tests passing. The main task-solving difference is that the parallel attempt spent its post-implementation window on a 15-child audit workflow and timed out at the process level, while the serial attempt completed the same kind of implementation and verification linearly and returned a final summary. That process difference did not produce a different delivered artifact outcome.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial left a detailed final explanation, while parallel final.txt is empty because the agent timed out.
Both used upstream Pallets Jinja as the baseline and made similar small hardening changes around import/export and test robustness.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; process contrast only
